item.description:
A tidy-up of Scribe's wording.

  • Em dashes in the app's text are now plain hyphens, including the bullets in What's New.
  • Smoothed the grammar of several messages, from the backlog's intro to Settings and the Save sheet.
  • Error messages for pieces that can't be opened now read like the rest of Scribe.

Updates now download by themselves and wait for a restart.

  • Scribe checks for a new version every time it opens, as well as once a day.
  • New versions download quietly in the background; a "Restart to update" button appears in the top bar when one is ready.
  • If you'd rather not restart yet, the update installs the next time you quit Scribe.

Scribe is ready to share: new libraries start clean, and updates back up your library first.

  • New libraries start with no categories. The welcome now asks what you read about and offers a dozen broad departments to start with: Science, History, Business, Maths and more.
  • Settings › Categories can add any of those starter departments later.
  • Before an update changes the database, Scribe copies it to the library's backups folder.
  • Help › Report a Bug… starts an email with the details that help fix a problem.
  • The About window credits the typefaces and open-source packages Scribe is built with.
  • Scribe asks to be moved to Applications if it's opened from somewhere it can't update itself.
  • Scribe checks for updates daily instead of hourly.
  • Scribe keeps to one window: File › New Window no longer opens a second copy, and ⌘N is just Save.
  • A new install no longer opens with "What's new" straight after the welcome.
